result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A gives a more complete page: it explains who each plan is for, has clear 'Start free trial' buttons, and suggests where real customer proof could go without making any up. However, A keeps the absolute 'no double-booking' claim in its hero and adds an unsupported 'instantly across all your channels' claim. B is cleaner on claims and keeps the details exactly, but it has no clear call-to-action button, gives little help choosing between plans, says nothing about real proof, and its notes wrongly say the features are framed as outcomes. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B gives a clearer page: each plan has a 'for whom' line, the page ends on a 'Start free trial' button, and it says what was cut and suggests adding a real customer quote without inventing one. However, B's headline and copy promise there will be no double-booking and add unbacked claims about instant syncing across all channels. A drops the hype more cleanly, but it doesn't help readers pick a plan, its explanation is generic, and it never suggests what proof the owner could add.
